cls: Hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor (HIF-PHI); oral anti-anaemic
pharm: Stabilises hypoxia-inducible factor by inhibiting prolyl hydroxylase, increasing endogenous erythropoietin and improving iron utilisation to raise haemoglobin in anaemia of chronic kidney disease
quick: 100 mg orally three times a week, titrated by haemoglobin response (per India label)
May be taken with or without food
Avoid - not recommended; insufficient data, HIF-PHI class caution
Used in CKD (dialysis and non-dialysis); titrate to haemoglobin
Use with caution; limited data in hepatic impairment
Haemoglobin, iron indices, blood pressure, thrombotic events
summary: Desidustat is an oral hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor (HIF-PHI) developed for the treatment of anaemia of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in both dialysis-dependent and non-dialysis-dependent patients. It was approved in India (2022) but is NOT FDA-approved; this record draws on the Indian approval, published trials (DREAM-D, DREAM-ND) and the established HIF-PHI class rather than a US label. By inhibiting prolyl hydroxylase, desidustat stabilises hypoxia-inducible factor, which upregulates endogenous erythropoietin production and genes governing iron absorption and mobilisation, raising haemoglobin while reducing hepcidin. A representative regimen is 100 mg orally three times weekly, titrated to haemoglobin response. As with the HIF-PHI class, attention is needed to cardiovascular and thromboembolic risk, blood-pressure control, adequate iron stores, and the theoretical concern of HIF-mediated effects; haemoglobin should not be raised excessively.
indications: Treatment of anaemia associated with chronic kidney disease in dialysis-dependent patients
Treatment of anaemia associated with chronic kidney disease in non-dialysis-dependent patients

dosage.d: 100 mg orally three times a week (per Indian approval), titrated to haemoglobin response
dosage.t: Three times weekly, with or without food
dosage.n: Adjust dose at intervals based on haemoglobin; avoid rapid rises

dosage.d: Titrate up or down by haemoglobin trend, avoiding haemoglobin overshoot
dosage.t: Reassess at defined intervals (e.g. every 4 weeks)
dosage.n: Ensure adequate iron stores before and during therapy

admin: Take orally three times a week, with or without food
Assess and replete iron stores before and during treatment for optimal response
Titrate the dose to maintain target haemoglobin and avoid excessive rises (overshoot)
Monitor blood pressure and treat hypertension
Evaluate for and minimise cardiovascular and thromboembolic risk factors
Follow the locally approved label (India) as the drug is not FDA-approved
moa: Desidustat reversibly inhibits prolyl hydroxylase domain (PHD) enzymes, the oxygen sensors that normally tag hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) alpha subunits for degradation. By inhibiting these enzymes, desidustat stabilises HIF-alpha, mimicking the body's response to hypoxia. Stabilised HIF activates transcription of erythropoietin and of genes that enhance iron absorption and mobilisation (and lower hepcidin), increasing endogenous erythropoietin in a more physiological, pulsatile manner than injected erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. The net effect is stimulation of erythropoiesis and improved iron utilisation, raising haemoglobin in anaemia of chronic kidney disease.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to desidustat or any excipient
relative: History of thromboembolic or major cardiovascular events

preg: There are insufficient data on desidustat in pregnancy and HIF pathway modulation raises theoretical developmental concerns. It is not recommended in pregnancy; use only if the benefit clearly outweighs the risk and no alternative is suitable.
lact: It is not known whether desidustat is excreted in human milk. Because of insufficient data, breastfeeding is best avoided during treatment.
renal: Desidustat is specifically used to treat the anaemia of chronic kidney disease, in both dialysis and non-dialysis patients, and does not require avoidance in renal impairment; dosing is guided by haemoglobin response rather than by renal function. Iron status should be optimised.
hepatic: Data in hepatic impairment are limited. As HIF-PHIs are hepatically metabolised, use with caution in significant hepatic impairment and monitor response and tolerability.

moderate: Oral iron and phosphate binders / polyvalent cation products - may reduce absorption; separate dosing as advised
Other agents that raise haemoglobin (erythropoiesis-stimulating agents) - additive effect; avoid combined use
Drugs affecting CYP/UGT metabolism - potential pharmacokinetic interactions (class consideration)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; separate from iron/cation-containing products
interactions.diagnostics: Raises haemoglobin and alters iron indices and hepcidin; monitor accordingly

serious: Thromboembolic events (deep vein thrombosis, vascular access thrombosis)
emergency: Acute thrombotic event (stroke, pulmonary embolism, MI)

monitoring: Haemoglobin at regular intervals, avoiding rapid increases or overshoot
Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation) and repletion as needed
Clinical surveillance for thrombotic and cardiovascular events
counsel: This oral medicine treats anaemia caused by kidney disease by boosting your body's own red-cell production
Take it three times a week as prescribed; it can be taken with or without food
Keep iron and other supplements separated from this medicine if advised, and continue any iron prescribed
Have regular blood tests to check your haemoglobin and iron levels
Report chest pain, sudden breathlessness, leg swelling or weakness on one side urgently (possible clot)
Tell your doctor if your blood pressure is high or hard to control
pk: Haemoglobin response develops over weeks of regular dosing
Plasma peak within a few hours of an oral dose
Short plasma half-life consistent with intermittent (thrice-weekly) dosing
Pharmacodynamic erythropoietic effect outlasts plasma exposure
Store as per manufacturer at controlled room temperature
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; approved in India (2022) - this record is based on the Indian label, DREAM-D/DREAM-ND trials and the HIF-PHI class, not a US label
Oral HIF-PHI alternative to injectable erythropoiesis-stimulating agents for anaemia of CKD
Works by stabilising HIF, raising endogenous erythropoietin and improving iron utilisation (lowers hepcidin)
Class risks include thromboembolism, hypertension and cardiovascular events - do not overshoot haemoglobin
Optimise iron stores for best response; separate from iron/phosphate binders
Usual regimen is intermittent (three times weekly) dosing titrated to haemoglobin
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day, but if it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed one - do not take two doses at once. Keep to your three-times-weekly schedule.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Overdose may lead to an excessive rise in haemoglobin with increased thrombotic risk and worsening hypertension. Withhold the drug, monitor haemoglobin and blood pressure, and provide supportive care; consider phlebotomy if haemoglobin is dangerously elevated.
